document.title: fix(upload): ignore SIGPIPE and drain rejected request bodies
document.summary: The Runtime Upload Listener sends with `MSG_NOSIGNAL` and checks every send, and after a 409 or 413 it keeps reading the request body before closing.
document.why: A client disconnecting mid-response can kill the whole VitaDeck process ([#64](source:s1)), and clients still sending an archive see a connection reset instead of the JSON error ([#79](source:s2)).

sources.title: Upload listener: SIGPIPE on client disconnect can kill the host process
sources.gist: No SIGPIPE handling and unchecked send() in http_server.c.

sources.title: Runtime Upload 409 reply closes the socket before reading the request body
sources.gist: Drain the body or reply with Connection: close and a short drain.

lookFor: [#64](source:s1) suggests adding the scratch curl harness from #62 as a CTest; it is not added, because a CTest binding a LAN port can raise the macOS firewall prompt on dev machines. The socketpair harness covers both fixes instead.

groups.title: Send without SIGPIPE
groups.why: Writing to a client that hung up raised SIGPIPE and killed the host ([#64](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `send_response` now goes through `send_all`, which passes `VD_MSG_NOSIGNAL` from `src/platform/socket.h` and stops at the first failed send.
lookFor: On Vita `VD_MSG_NOSIGNAL` is 0 because the Vita headers have no `MSG_NOSIGNAL` and sceNet never raises SIGPIPE; only the Docker Vita build proves this compiles.
When the 200 reply fails to send, the package is still published and the Shell still sees the success; only the client misses the JSON.

groups.title: Drain the body after 409 and 413
groups.why: Closing while the client still sends makes it see a reset instead of the JSON error ([#79](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `drain_rejected_request` runs after the 409 and 413 replies in `handle_upload`: it shuts down the write side, then reads up to one maximum-size request with a 2 second `SO_RCVTIMEO`, and the harness proves a 1MB body can finish sending.
lookFor: Subtle: the 413 drain runs while that request still holds the ingest lock, so another upload during the drain (up to 16MB, or until 2 quiet seconds) gets 409.
The reply goes out before the drain, so curl with `Expect: 100-continue` gets the 413 at once and never sends the body; the drain then ends on its EOF.
`upload_once` in the harness now shuts down its write side, or every 413 case there would wait out the 2 second drain timeout.

commits.subject: fix(upload): drain the body before closing a 409 or 413
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The single-flight 409 and the over-limit 413 replied and closed while the client was still sending, so curl and Node fetch often saw a connection reset instead of the JSON error. After those replies the handler now shuts down its write side and reads up to one maximum-size request, giving up after 2 quiet seconds.

Fixes #79

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(upload): send without SIGPIPE and stop a reply on send failure
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A client hanging up mid-response raised SIGPIPE and killed the host. Sends now pass MSG_NOSIGNAL (src/platform/socket.h; sceNet never raises SIGPIPE), loop over partial writes, and skip the body once the header send fails.

Fixes #64

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
